strengths: Clear motivation addressing fundamental limitations of clustering-based and 2D lifting-based part segmentation methods, with effective visual demonstrations (Figures 2, 9)

weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: dual-branch encoder combines existing PartField components with learnable variant, mask decoder is straightforward SAM adaptation, triplane representation from prior work. Incomplete analysis of frozen branch contribution: Table 3 shows only ~5 IoU gap between learnable and dual-branch variants; limited investigation of which 2D priors most benefit part understanding; missing ablation on frozen branch importance

Evaluation methodology issues: disabling mesh connectivity for PartField creates unfair comparison as Table 4 shows connectivity provides 51.5→79.2 boost; performance gaps widen on 3DCoMPaT++ fine-grained annotations, suggesting scalability challenges

Limited failure case analysis: Figure 14 shows failures on engraved surfaces and unstructured objects but lacks quantitative analysis; no breakdown of failure rates by object category; long-tail part distribution mentioned but not addressed

Practical limitations: Cannot produce semantic labels limiting downstream applicability; NMS threshold in automatic mode requires tuning with no principled guidance; requires 8 H20 GPUs; no analysis of performance degradation with lower input resolutions

Dataset and generalization concerns: Training data from Objaverse/artist assets with limited diversity compared to 2D SAM's billion-scale dataset; evaluation primarily on synthetic shapes and high-quality scans; limited testing on low-quality/noisy real-world data; no cross-domain evaluation

Technical clarity: Triplet contrastive loss formulation not detailed; mechanism for incorporating previous prompts appears ad-hoc; limited justification for why triplane specifically vs. other continuous representations; hyperparameter choices (α=2, λ=0.5) lack principled justification

Missing comparisons: No evaluation against semantic segmentation methods adapted for parts; limited exploration of other 2D foundation models beyond SAM; Point-SAM trained on authors' data (Table 3) is useful but Point-SAM wasn't designed for native 3D supervision
Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned; unclear if 500k curated dataset will be released; dependency on Objaverse and licensed datasets may limit reproducibility
